patterns.name: Legacy System Decommissioning Gap
patterns.description: Improperly decommissioned cloud resources create persistent security vulnerabilities that can be exploited years after initial deployment

incident_example.vulnerability: Legacy third-party cloud file storage from 2020 not properly decommissioned
incident_example.impact: Affected <25% of merchant base, internal operational documents accessed
incident_example.response: Refused ransom, donated equivalent amount to cybersecurity research labs

practices: Automated alerts for unused resources (>90 days)

cost_of_failure: Reputational damage and customer trust erosion

applicability_to_chained.reasoning: Multiple legacy resources likely exist from early development phases (2024-2025)
risk_areas: Old Cloud Storage buckets from experiments
Deprecated service accounts with lingering permissions
Archived Cloud SQL snapshots with sensitive data
Legacy Cloud Run revisions with outdated configs
applicability_to_chained.recommended_action: Immediate GCP resource audit and cleanup

monitoring.automation: Weekly automated audits via GitHub Actions

patterns.name: Hidden Multi-Cloud Data Transfer Costs
patterns.description: Internet egress charges can equal or exceed compute costs in multi-cloud architectures, creating unexpected bill shock

example.problem: MongoDB Atlas costs reached $3,000+/month for a few hundred GB
example.root_cause: Multi-cloud architecture required internet data transfer ($1,000/month = 33% of total)

architectural_principles: Keep all services in same cloud region
Implement aggressive caching for external APIs
Use Cloud CDN for static content delivery
monitoring: Track internet egress costs (alert if >10% of total)
Monitor external API call volume and costs

applicability_to_chained.current_status: SAFE - all services in us-west1 region, single GCP cloud
risk_areas: External API calls (GitHub API, Gemini API) over internet
Future multi-region expansion could introduce transfer costs
Blog content delivery from Cloud Storage (currently minimal)
applicability_to_chained.recommended_action: Implement cost monitoring, baseline current data transfer

decision_criteria.consider_multi_cloud: Costs >$1,000/month AND need for geographic distribution

patterns.name: Self-Hosting for Cost Optimization at Scale
patterns.description: Mature workloads can achieve 60-90% cost reduction through self-hosting on lower-tier providers like Hetzner
benefits: Massive cost savings (90% observed in Prosopo case)
Full control over infrastructure and configuration
No vendor lock-in, easier to migrate
drawbacks: Less agile for rapid feature development

hetzner.pricing: 90% cheaper than AWS/GCP for equivalent specs

applicability_to_chained.current_assessment: Too early - rapid development phase, costs <$400/month
reasoning: Chained is still evolving rapidly (frequent feature changes)
Current GCP costs well below $1,000/month threshold
Managed services (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL) provide critical auto-scaling
Team focused on AI/ML development, not infrastructure management
applicability_to_chained.recommended_action: Monitor costs quarterly, revisit in Q2 2026 if costs spike

actionable_recommendations.description: Audit all GCP resources, identify unused/legacy items, document decommissioning process

expected_impact.security: HIGH - eliminate legacy system attack surface

actionable_recommendations.description: Create automated cost tracking, set up billing alerts, establish baseline
Create standard processes for resource creation, review, and decommissioning
Research Go-based infrastructure tools for future use

phase_1.name: Monitor
actions: Identify top 3 cost drivers (Cloud Run, Storage, SQL likely)
Export cost data to learnings/ directory

phase_2.name: Quick Wins
actions: Implement lifecycle policies (Coldline for old data)

phase_3.name: Strategic Optimization
actions: If data transfer >$100: Optimize external API usage
Consider reserved instances for stable workloads

key_takeaways: Legacy systems are security landmines - active decommissioning is critical, not optional
Data transfer costs can exceed compute costs - multi-cloud has hidden price tags
Self-hosting can save 90% but requires stable workloads and DevOps expertise
Transparency in incident response builds trust - Checkout.com's response exemplary
Cloud-native is evolving but complexity is real - evaluate against actual needs
